claim: Zika virus was introduced into Brazil and Haiti in 2014.
source: In 2014, Zika virus was introduced into Brazil and Haiti, from where it rapidly spread throughout the Americas.
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text without supporting data or citations provided in this specific sentence.

claim: By January 2017, over 100,000 Zika cases had been confirmed in 24 different states in Brazil.
source: By January 2017, over 100,000 cases had been confirmed in 24 different states in Brazil (http://ais.paho.org/phip/viz/ed_zika_cases.asp), with large numbers of reports from many other counties in South and Central America (Faria et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by a web database citation and a scholarly reference (Faria et al., 2016).

claim: Zika virus was originally isolated in Uganda in 1947.
source: Originally isolated in Uganda in 1947, the virus remained poorly understood until it began to spread within the South Pacific, including an outbreak affecting 75% of the residents on the island of Yap in 2007 (49 confirmed cases) and over 32,000 cases in the rest of Oceania in 2013–2014, the largest outbreak prior to the Americas (2016-present) (Cao-Lormeau et al., 2016; Duffy et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to Cao-Lormeau et al., 2016 and Duffy et al., 2009.

claim: An outbreak on the island of Yap in 2007 affected 75% of residents with 49 confirmed cases.
source: Originally isolated in Uganda in 1947, the virus remained poorly understood until it began to spread within the South Pacific, including an outbreak affecting 75% of the residents on the island of Yap in 2007 (49 confirmed cases) and over 32,000 cases in the rest of Oceania in 2013–2014, the largest outbreak prior to the Americas (2016-present) (Cao-Lormeau et al., 2016; Duffy et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to Cao-Lormeau et al., 2016 and Duffy et al., 2009.

claim: Over 32,000 Zika cases occurred in Oceania in 2013-2014, representing the largest outbreak prior to the Americas.

evidence: Supported by citations to Cao-Lormeau et al., 2016 and Duffy et al., 2009.

claim: In February 2016, the World Health Organization declared the American Zika virus epidemic to be a Public Health Emergency of International Concern.

claim: Aedes aegypti and Ae. albopictus are presumed to be the primary vectors of Zika virus due to epidemiologic association.
source: It has been presumed that Aedes aegypti and Ae. albopictus are the primary vectors due to epidemiologic association with Zika virus (Messina et al., 2016), viral isolation from and transmission experiments with field populations (especially in Ae. aegypti [Haddow et al., 2012; Boorman and Porterfield, 1956; Haddow et al., 1964]), and association with related arboviruses (e.g. dengue fever virus, yellow fever virus).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations including Messina et al., 2016, Haddow et al., 2012, Boorman and Porterfield, 1956, and Haddow et al., 1964.

claim: Viral isolation from and transmission experiments with field populations support Ae. aegypti as a Zika vector.
